chapter: Will Marion Cook and the Southern Syncopated Orchestra
title: The train accident that killed Mope Desmond
summary: On a train to a hunting-party ball a loose footplate from a passing express smashed through the compartment and killed Desmond; the club took care of his family.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: And we were sent out by the Club to Wolverhampton, or something, I think, to play for a hunting party or something, the ball of a hunting party, or something.

And we left, Mope Desmond, who was in charge of the business, was at the station, and two of the boys were late, so he left the tickets of two of them with the booking office, for the boys, with a porter or someone.
Then I left with him. He, George Hines, Mope and I, we went ahead in the first train. We were taking a train and I left word for the boys to take another train to get there and everything.
And it so happened -- I'll explain to you very exactly, what happened. I'd have to show you what happened, because this is tragic. It was tragic.
Briggs 124
You see, the compartment, the train compartment, this represents the other side of the compartment. This represents the seat going that way. And this spacing goes like that.
Right, right.
Desmond, he preferred to sit. We clashed pretty often about the seat. That's a funny thing, because I wanted to sit this way, so I could see better, I guess.
Right.

And he got it there, and he fell over on my knees.
He just fell straight forward, right onto your knees.
That's right.

Yes, he fell over my knees, and he died about five minutes after.
That's a terrible story.

Terrible story. And that was the reason why both Patrick and I go to the Club rooms. They were simply terrific with us.
